results.note: Degrade-not-raise guard weakened: a non-dict 'settings' (a list or string) slips past and reaches the dict comprehension instead of returning the packaging-slip reason.
None-vs-truthiness slip: filters on truthiness rather than string type, so non-string prose values are admitted into the explanation table.
Dropped normalization: a whitespace-only explanation counts as explained, so the replacement for the old TypeError-at-import check stops catching blank prose.
Swapped return values: the documented (unexplained, orphan) tuple order is reversed, so callers report each gap as the other kind.
Missing-prose fallback becomes the setting name instead of empty, so every consumer believes an unexplained setting is explained and the 'explanation unavailable' path never fires.
Sentence split loses the space requirement, so an explanation containing an abbreviation, a version number or a filename is truncated at the first period.
Boundary flip: a gist exactly `width` characters long is needlessly truncated instead of printed whole.
Word-boundary trim uses the first space rather than the last, collapsing the gist to a single word.
None-vs-truthiness: an empty-string setting name skips the unknown-setting error and falls through to the index instead of exiting EXIT_ERROR.
Console detection inverted: redirected or piped output gets the abbreviated index while a terminal gets the full dump -- exactly backwards from the documented policy.
Dropped .strip() on the opt-out env var, so a value with surrounding whitespace no longer suppresses the prompt.
Wrong stream checked before prompting: stdin availability is never verified, so input() is called with no console attached to read from.
